groups.defect: The update-only path treats stale existing devices as over-limit new devices, returning ErrDeviceLimitReached and rejecting their authentication.
groups.rationale: Both report the same rejection of an existing device whose stored updated_at falls outside the update window when the limit is reached.

groups.defect: The non-atomic count-and-insert sequence allows concurrent new devices to exceed the configured limit.
groups.rationale: All three identify the same race between CountDevices and the subsequent insert, with equivalent concurrent-request examples.

groups.defect: Caching a device before its database write succeeds leaves failed registrations cached for 29 minutes, allowing retries to bypass device-limit rejection.
groups.rationale: All three explicitly identify the same premature SetDefault call in tagDeviceUI. The bypass reports explain the authentication consequence of the stale cache entry reported by the shorter suggestion.

groups.defect: Returning an untyped ErrDeviceLimitReached from Authenticate produces a generic authentication error rather than a controlled quota response.
groups.rationale: Both report the missing translation of the limit sentinel into an error carrying an appropriate HTTP status and message. The synchronous tagging change is context for this defect.
